problem:
A concrete block of mass $15\,\text{kg}$ is released vertically downward with an initial velocity of $1\,\text{m/s}.$ Let $v(t)$ be the block's velocity, in meters per second, $t\ge 0$ seconds after release, with downward taken as the positive direction. The air resistance on the block is proportional to the square of its velocity with a constant of proportionality $k=1.47\,\text{kg/m}$ and acts in the direction opposite to motion.

Find, rounded to two decimal places, the velocity of the block after $1$ second.
Assume the acceleration due to gravity is $g=9.8\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ and the only forces acting on the block are the weight due to gravity and drag.
worked_solution:
First, note that only two forces act on the block: the force due to gravity, given by the weight

$$
w=mg=15g
$$

and the force due to drag $D,$ which is proportional to the velocity squared (and negative since it acts in the negative direction):

$$
D=-k{v}^{2}=-1.47{v}^{2}
$$

Hence, the resultant force acting on the block is

$$
F=w+D=15g-1.47{v}^{2}.
$$

Applying Newton's second law, we obtain a separable first-order differential equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\ 15g-1.47{v}^{2} & =15\,\frac{dv}{dt} \\ \frac{dv}{dt} & =g-0.098{v}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dv}{dt} & =g(1-0.01{v}^{2}) \\ \frac{1}{1-0.01{v}^{2}}\cdot \frac{dv}{dt} & =g \\ \int \frac{1}{1-0.01{v}^{2}}\cdot \frac{dv}{dt}\,dt & =g\int dt \\ \int \frac{1}{1-(0.1v)^{2}}\,dv & =g\int dt \\ \frac{1}{0.1}\operatorname{artanh}⁡(0.1v) & =gt+{C}_{1} \\ \operatorname{artanh}⁡(0.1v) & =\frac{1}{10}gt+C \\ 0.1v & =\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{1}{10}gt+C) \\ v(t) & =10\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{1}{10}gt+C),\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=0.1{C}_{1}$ is a constant of integration.

We're told that the block is released with an initial velocity of $1\,\text{m/s}.$ So, we can apply the initial condition $v(0)=1,$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =10\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{1}{10}g\cdot 0+C) \\ 1 & =10\operatorname{tanh}⁡(C) \\ \operatorname{tanh}⁡(C) & =0.1 \\ C & =\operatorname{artanh}⁡(0.1)≈0.100\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following expression for $v(t):$

$$
v(t)=10\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{1}{10}gt+0.100)
$$

Finally, the velocity of the block after $t=1$ second is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =10\operatorname{tanh}⁡(\frac{1}{10}\cdot 9.8\cdot 1+0.100) \\  & =10\operatorname{tanh}⁡(0.98+0.100) \\  & =7.931\,99… \\  & ≈7.93\,\text{m/s},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
